messages.subject: Re: secrlinear GoF testing
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sean
I assume we are talking here about secr.test(). I don't remember specifically implementing that for linear data, but it might be interesting to pin down where it comes adrift and whether it is easily fixed. The error you are getting comes from sim.detect() that is called by simulate.secr() early in a call to secr.test(). I'll try to check it in the next day or so. If the worst comes to the worst you can replicate the behaviour of secr.test easily enough by simulating your own linear data via sim.linearpopn and sim.capthist (see secrlinear-vignette.pdf <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/secrlinear/vignettes/secrlinear-vignette.pdf>).
Murray

I think you got needlessly tangled up here. Do not put your data in the package extdata folder. The example in secr-datainput.pdf <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-datainput.pdf> goes there just to retrieve some demo data that is distributed with the package. messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am running secr density analyses for four different areas within a reserve. Three of the areas have worked perfectly, however, the analyses for the one area keeps giving me the following error: "Error in as.vector(data) :  no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector".

Example code:

BH_Muz <- read.capthist('Capture_mazunga.csv', 'TrapDepMazunga.csv' , detector = "proximity", fmt = "trapID", trapcovnames =c('habitat', 'site', 'lion', 'leopard', 'spottedhyaena'))

closure.test(BH_Muz, SB=FALSE, min.expected = 2)

maskMuz <- boundary <- readOGR(".", "BHmaskMuz")
BHmaskMuz <- make.mask(traps(BH_Muz),type="polygon", poly=maskMuz, poly.habitat = TRUE)

Following models do give the error:
#spottedhyaena+lion+habitat
secrspottedhyaenalionhabitat <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~spottedhyaena + lion + habitat, mask=maskMuz, verify = FALSE)

#spottedhyaena+lion
secrspottedhyaenalion <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~spottedhyaena + lion, mask=maskMuz, verify = FALSE)

#leopard+lion+habitat
secrleopardlionhabitat <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~leopard + lion + habitat, mask=maskMuz, verify = FALSE)

Following models do not give the error:
#leopard+lion
secrleopardlion <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~leopard + lion, mask=BHmaskMuz, verify = FALSE)

#spottedhyaena+leopard
secrspottedhyaenaleopard <- secr.fit(BH_Muz, model = g0~spottedhyaena + leopard, mask=maskMuz, verify = FALSE)

Any advice will be greatly appreciated.

All the best,
Jess

messages.subject_clean: no method for coercing this S4 class to a vector
messages.body_plain:
That's a puzzle. I wonder if the code you present is really the code you used. Certainly, it seems unlikely that the secrspottedhyaenaleopard model actually fitted if you really gave the raw (SpatialPolygons?) result from readOGR as the mask. S4 objects are used by package 'sp', 'rgdal' etc. for SpatialPolygons etc., but very little by 'secr' itself. So the problem almost certainly has to do with misuse of the polygon data.
Murray

messages.subject: openCR 2.1.0
messages.body_plain:
openCR 2.1.0 is now available on CRAN, including the Windows binary. This version fixes the bug that blocked 'derived' (thanks Trent) and adds quite a few extras for movement modelling. Check here <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/openCR%202.1.0%20NEWS.txt> and read the vignette <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/openCR-vignette.pdf> for specifics. The default maximum number of iterations in openCR.fit() has been increased to 300, which should reduce the frequency of 'code 4' results.
Murray

I am trying to use run.scenarios to test different potential trap layouts. I have a list of 100 trap objects (in object test) that I pulled from a list of potential camera locations (cams).

I thought I could use a list of trap objects in run.scenarios to run through each item in the list, but I am doing something incorrectly, and cannot figure out how to loop through each trap layout. Could someone inform me if there is a function in secr or secrdesign that can test multiple different scenarios like run.scenarios, or help me figure out how to get run.scenarios to work on a list of trap objects?

cams <- read.traps(file = "\~SWarea_locs.txt", detector = "proximity")
test <- purrr::map(1:100, ~ sample_n(cams, 50), .id = "subset") # creates 100 lists of 50 random camera locations in df

#Count clusters and make that nrepeats

messages.body_plain:
This is certainly a task for secrdesign. Is it simply that in make.scenarios() 'trapsindex' should be an integer variable, an index to the list rather than the list itself? I suggest trapsindex = 1:length(test). It's probably a lot simpler to allow run.scenarios to construct masks as needed (using a buffer multiplier xsigma) rather than explicitly providing a list of masks, but that may not apply. Do try run.scenarios() first with fit = FALSE, or simply use scenarioSummary() to check out your scenarios.
'secrdesign' is not easy!
Murray

> A multisession analysis allows you to fit a model with each detection parameter (g0 or lambda0 and sigma) held at the same value across years (e.g. g0~1, sigma~1).
